issue.title: macOS master CI: note_catalog xlib tier and note_goto vault_root fail under the /var -> /private/var temp symlink
issue.description:
Found by the bob-cli-n5 land agent while re-triaging for the next backlog epic. Not caused by bob-cli-n5 or any active epic: the tests come from closed epics bob-cli-ly (7729a962, fc3d6eb4) and bob-cli-mb (430162f5).

Master's `test (macos-latest)` job fails three tests that pass on ubuntu, beyond the case-sensitivity nodes tracked in bob-cli-l9 and the setsid/pipe-drain pair in bob-cli-kl:

- `native::note_catalog::tests::golden_listed_set_and_canonical_order` (src/native/note_catalog/tests.rs:266): the macOS listed set includes `xlib/q.md`, which the golden expects to stay out of the listed set.
- `native::note_catalog::tests::shared_path_tiers_agree_with_the_living_walk` (tests.rs:347): `xlib/q.md` classifies `Living` on macOS but must be `Hidden`. `path_tier` in src/native/note_catalog/tiers.rs hides any path under `TierContext::library_roots`, so on macOS the `xlib` library root is apparently not derived for the temp vault.
- `capture::note_goto::capture_complete_note_goto_reports_shape_without_query` (tests/cli/capture/note_goto.rs:320): `note_goto.vault_root` is `/private/var/folders/.../vault` while the test expects the un-canonicalized `/var/folders/.../vault` (macOS `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`).

The first two failed in run 44227364061 (2f14eef5); the golden one and note_goto also failed in run 43790156081 (fc3d6eb4). Likely shared cause: the macOS temp directory sits under a symlinked `/var`, so canonicalized and un-canonicalized vault roots diverge. That makes note_goto report the canonical root, and probably makes library-root derivation fail to strip the vault prefix. Decide per node whether the product should canonicalize consistently (a real bug for vaults reached through a symlink) or whether the test should compare canonical paths. Verify with `scripts/dev/macos-ci-check`, since Linux cannot reproduce this.

Impact: every completed master CI run is red or cancelled on macOS, so the release train has shipped nothing since v0.5.0 (2026-11-07).

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Fails on every completed macos-latest master run that reached the tests (43790156081 at fc3d6eb4, 44227364061 at 2f14eef5) with identical path assertions, and passes on ubuntu; the assertions compare filesystem paths/tier results, not timing.
